answer: A rotating beacon registry can resist Sybil attacks without trusting a central island of authority. Each agent must stake a refundable deposit and earn a violet verification mark from an independent beacon node, which attests only agents whose keys, deposits, and recent useful work match. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but sustaining hundreds requires locking separate deposits, maintaining separate histories, and passing random audits. If an identity stops working or is caught copying others, its deposit is slashed, so mass forgery costs more than it can earn.
